evals.name: missed-caller
evals.prompt: I just finished the work on this branch and I want to merge it into main. Can you check it for any bugs or regressions before I open the PR?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that src/receipt.js still reads p.total after pricing() renamed the field to grandTotal, causing a crash/undefined at runtime; notes the test suite passes and therefore does not catch it. Reports as a high-severity regression with receipt.js and a fix (read p.grandTotal).
assertions: Identifies src/receipt.js as still reading the removed .total field (the missed caller)
Flags the receipt.js issue as high severity / blocking (not a minor nit)
Notes the test suite passes yet does not cover receipt.js, so tests miss the bug
Suggests fixing receipt.js to read p.grandTotal
Does not raise high-severity findings on the correct checkout.js or pricing.js

evals.name: removed-guard
evals.prompt: Review my current branch for bugs before I merge. Did I break anything?
evals.expected_output: Runs the test suite, sees ZeroDivisionError from average([]) after the empty-input guard was removed, and reports it as a high-severity regression tied to the removed guard in stats.py with a fix (restore the guard).
assertions: Actually runs the test suite (unittest/pytest/make test) and references its output
Identifies the ZeroDivisionError / crash on empty input to average()
Attributes the failure to the removed empty-input guard in stats.py
Suggests restoring the guard / handling the empty-list case

evals.name: clean-refactor
evals.prompt: Is this branch safe to merge? Check it for regressions.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the formatName refactor preserves behavior, confirms tests pass, and reports the branch as safe to merge with no manufactured findings.
assertions: Concludes the branch is safe to merge / reports no regressions
Confirms the tests were run and pass
Does not manufacture high-severity findings on the behavior-preserving refactor
